pairs.why: A's chunky, smoothly shaded stone with big readable checker squares matches the real card better than B's veined, slightly more realistic marble.
A has the chunkier stone, bigger board squares and smoother finish of the real table, while B has more marble texture and a finer, busier grid.
B's slightly larger squares and rounder, chunkier pedestal sit a little closer to the real table, but the two drawings are nearly equal.
A's thick, rounded body and plain house emblem are a little closer to the real unit's soft, chunky build than B's crisper, thinner casing.
A keeps the real card's thick, rounded casing, while B is thinner and flatter and leans more toward a realistic product shot.
B is a single clean unit on a striped wall like the real card, while A adds a busy room (plant, books, sofa, window) and a glowing LED strip the real card doesn't have.
B shows a big, close-up, chunky lamp whose three colored lenses fill the front like the real card, while A's lamp is small and distant with long, washed-out beams.
A's grey metal truss and simple dark lamp body match the real card, while B adds a navy truss and yellow bolt accents that aren't on the real card.
